messages:
Alex: thinking out loud — trying a different canary ramp pattern for model swaps. instead of big linear steps, what about a pulsed microstep schedule (short bursts then hold) so we get fast signals + cache warmup without blasting traffic all at once?
Maya: can you sketch the config? sounds promising for cache warmup + KV cache priming.
Alex: sure — prototype YAML below for discussion:
```yaml
rollout:
  mode: pulsed            # pulsed | linear | exponential
  pulse_percent: 3       # each mini-burst percent of total traffic
  pulses_per_step: 4     # number of pulses before a longer hold window
  pulse_duration: 30     # seconds per pulse
  hold_seconds: 300      # hold after pulses to aggregate telemetry
  max_percent: 30        # upper bound for the canary
  safety:
    p95_latency_increase: 0.25   # fraction (25%)
    error_rate_absolute: 0.5     # percent absolute threshold
    rollback_on: ["error_rate", "response_quality_regression"]
  cohorts:
    - name: baseline
      selectors: ["control", "not_premium"]
    - name: premium_warmup
      selectors: ["premium_users"]
  sampling:
    eval_sample_rate: 0.01   # override sampling during canary windows
  quota_behavior: sticky   # sticky | soft | isolated
```
Maya: interesting — pulses_per_step 4 + pulse_duration 30s = 2min pulses then 5m hold? need to be explicit about total window math.
Sam: if pulse_duration is short we can get a fast signal then hold for aggregation. important: define aggregation window (rolling 1m vs 5m) for each metric.
Julie: main concerns: quota accounting (we bill tokens) and cohort leakage. how do we guarantee premium cohorts don't get traffic bleed and double billing?
Alex: plan is to pin cohort selection before routing and use sticky routing keys for 24h. quotas tracked per route-id/model-version so billing attribution stays clear.
Ben: telemetry Q: do we rely only on request logs or also sample outputs for quality evals? today sampling is 1/1000, we should bump to 1/100 for canaries.
Maya: agree — add sample_override: 0.01 and a flag to mark samples as canary to prioritize them in eval pipelines.
Sam: API design debate: expose low-level pulse primitives in the platform API, or have console produce them from a high-level slider? i prefer API-first + console helper. keeps integrations clean.
Julie: UI must show expected traffic curve and a predicted cost delta. PMs will ask if spikes are expected. visualizing pulses and hold windows helps communication.
Alex: also propose a guard: graceful-fallback to previous model variant on sustained error, with a cooldown/backoff that ramps down slowly to avoid thrash (e.g., rollback -> 10% immediate -> decay 2%/min until stable).
canary-bot: [deploy] starting pulsed rollout for model redwood-13b@v2 -> pulses: 3% x4 every 30s, hold 5m, max 30%.
Alex: PoC on staging tomorrow. volunteers to review schema + telemetry hooks?
Maya: I'll own telemetry hooks and sampling changes.
Sam: I'll draft API proto and open PR for the pulse primitives.
Julie: I'll mock up console visuals + a compact runbook explaining the hold/rollback semantics.
Ben: I'll update quota counters and make sure billing attribution is per-route-id.
Alex: great — once PRs land we'll run a small internal canary and gather notes. thanks :thumbsup:
